chunks: And if they had been pleased with what God and His Messenger had given them, and said: 'God is sufficient for us; He will give us of His largesse as will His Apostle. We supplicate no one but God.'
ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Hasbuna Allah' signify in terms of reliance and supplication?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the event of the Hijr (seclusion) of Imam Ali (AS) or the general attitude of the faithful during times of hardship, emphasizing *rida* (contentment) with divine decree. It underscores the principle of *kifayah* (God's sufficiency), where believers reject worldly dependencies and direct their ultimate longing (*raghibun*) solely to Allah, reflecting the spiritual station of the Ahl al-Bayt.
